newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Former Murdoch headquarters gutted by fire.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Former Murdoch headquarters gutted by fire.

text.p: The building from which Rupert Murdoch launched his global media empire 40 years ago was destroyed on Wednesday in a fire.

Murdoch began his career as a newspaper proprietor in the 1950s in the four-storey building in this South Australia city which had been the headquarters of a stable of newspapers belonging to his father, Sir Keith Murdoch.
Witnesses said the now-vacant building caught fire at five p.m. (0630 GMT). Twenty fire engines and 50 firefighters were unable to stop the blaze which spread to a nearby hotel.
"We have no cause and we have no estimates of damage at this stage," a fire brigade spokesman told Reuters.
But he said the fire brigade had been called to the building "numerous times" in recent weeks to put out small fires believed to have been started by squatters trying to keep warm.

The art deco-style grey stone building, built in 1924, was home to the The News, Rupert Murdoch's first newspaper, which closed down in 1994. Murdoch's Australian media subsidiary, News Limited, moved its Adelaide operations in 1987, former employees said on Wednesday.
The building, on North Terrace in central Adelaide, had been vacant for some years. It was recently announced that a Malaysian consortium would redevelop it as a hotel.
Murdoch, now a U.S. citzen, heads the global media group News Corp, which has interests worldwide in films, television, publishing and newspapers.
